recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-41852 unless a future work group decision reopens the broader CodeableReference constraint policy.
issue_request: FHIR-41852 was an Applied FHIR-core R5 change request resolved Persuasive for R6. It observed that the CodeableReference narrative already used SHALL NOT for targetProfile and binding constraints on child elements, making the sentence about evaluating a future change from SHOULD NOT to SHALL NOT obsolete; the requested change was to remove that sentence.
initial_application: The obsolete sentence was introduced by d621ab0bda61832d87d16ee8fa98261bf403a9da for FHIR-30877. FHIR-39176 later changed the main CodeableReference rule from SHOULD NOT to SHALL NOT, leaving the future-evaluation sentence stale. Git history contains a FHIR-41852 commit, ea8157b624fe388cb51df371d2b63d251cd6922d, that removed the stale sentence, but it is not an ancestor of the current reconciliation branch. The current branch already has the same cleanup through 00fb2e6c6f2c647fdd737a71923ced387f84a93a for FHIR-40955.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists CodeableReference as a datatype and maps codeablereference to the references page, so source/references.html is current build-scoped source for the affected narrative. Current source/references.html keeps the SHALL NOT rule and no longer contains the stale future-evaluation sentence. A later FHIR-38957 reconciliation clarified the same paragraph's targetProfile/binding wording without reintroducing the obsolete sentence. FHIR-I minutes from 2023-12-18 record the FHIR-41852 Persuasive vote, and no Zulip discussion or conflicting community evidence was found.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current active CodeableReference narrative already implements FHIR-41852's requested deletion.
